candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — healthy nursing work environment and meaningful recognition
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize meaningful staff recognition as an AACN healthy-work-environment practice that acknowledges individual contributions and supports a sense of value and fulfillment without replacing other workplace standards.

options.A: It is primarily a disciplinary process for identifying staff members who do not meet productivity expectations.
options.B: It replaces the need for appropriate staffing, skilled communication, collaboration, decision making, and leadership.
options.C: It should be limited to executives because bedside and peer recognition do not contribute to a healthy work environment.
options.D: It acknowledges the value of team members' contributions in ways that are meaningful to them and can strengthen fulfillment within a healthy work environment.

candidate.rationale: AACN lists Meaningful Recognition as one of six standards for a healthy work environment. The standard requires nurses to be recognized and to recognize others for the value each brings to the organization's work, and AACN describes individualized, meaningful recognition as supporting a sense of value and nurse fulfillment. D reflects this standard. Recognition does not replace the other healthy-work-environment standards, is not primarily disciplinary, and is intended to reach from bedside to boardroom rather than executives alone.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AACN requires meaningful recognition of the value team members bring to the organization; recognition should be individualized and meaningful and can enhance a sense of value and fulfillment.
candidate.source_document_title: Meaningful Recognition — AACN Healthy Work Environments
